title: Lit Bulbs
statement:
A row of light bulbs is described by one number: write the number in **binary**, and every digit 1 is a bulb that is on, every digit 0 is a bulb that is off. For example 13 is `1101` in binary, so three bulbs are on.

For each of the **t** given numbers, print how many bulbs are on, that is, how many 1-bits the number has.
input:
The first line contains an integer **t**.

The second line contains t integers x[1], ..., x[t].
output: Print t lines. Line i contains the number of 1-bits of x[i].
hints: `x & 1` is the lowest bit, and `x >> 1` shifts all bits one place to the right.
A neat trick: `x & (x - 1)` removes the lowest 1-bit. Count how many times you can do it before x becomes 0.
editorial:
Look at the bits one by one: add `x & 1` to the answer and shift x right until it becomes 0. Values reach 10^18, so use an unsigned or signed 64-bit type. C++ also has `__builtin_popcountll(x)`, Java has `Long.bitCount(x)` and Python has `bin(x).count('1')`.

Complexity: O(60) per number.
